newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Mayr-Melnhof posts 34 pct rise in final 1996 net.
newsitem.headline: Mayr-Melnhof posts 34 pct rise in final 1996 net.

text.p: Austrian cartonboard maker Mayr-Melnhof on Wednesday posted a 34 percent rise in final 1996 net profit to 448 million schillings, its best result since the group went public in 1994.
Pretax profit went up to 699 million schillings from 430 million a year ago. Mayr-Melnhof said it would pay a dividend of 17 schillings for 1996 after paying no dividend the previous year.
Mayr-Melnhof said final 1996 sales had fallen to 10.497 billion schillings from 12.253 billion a year earlier.
The group blamed the decline on lower cartonboard and waste paper prices as well as a higher proportion of internal sales resulting from increased integration between divisions.

Mayr-Melnhof declined to provide a detailed outlook for the current year but said it expected "stable demand" for its products. "The return on sales of the group should be in the same region as last year," it added.
Mayr-Melnhof is Europe's leading cartonboard manufacturer. Over the past year, it expanded in India, Singapore, Britain, and Eastern Europe.

Last month, the group said it had completed the purchase of Reynolds International's packaging plant in southern Germany. The expansion into cigarette packaging would bring in extra sales of about 1.5 billion schillings, MMK said without giving a time period.
